claim: But the EU and the US both demand 85%, so almost every Chilean bottle you will ever see is made to 85%
because: 27 CFR 4.23(b) sets the US minimum for a single-variety name at 75%, and it applies to imported wine as well as domestic wine (51% for labrusca). The 85% figure is the EU rule. It is not a US rule.
fix: But the EU demands 85% (the US, like Chile, takes 75%), so wine bound for Europe, and much Chilean export wine besides, is made to 85%. That is why the textbook figure and the shelf reality can disagree. Quote the law, then note the export practice.
